expected.judge_guidance: G5 does the heavy lifting; the judge checks the prose carries the same honesty as the structured fields. Rolling must read as rolling, with the quarterly-trustees citation put to use ('apply ahead of the next quarterly meeting') rather than a vague 'no deadline'. Undisclosed amount must read as 'amount not disclosed by the funder', never an estimate or a 'typically' figure (the must_not_mention canaries). Between-rounds must read as 'opens October 2026 - prepare now' and never as open-now. A 5 turns each absence into usable advice; a 3 merely avoids fabricating; inventing any number or date is a gate failure, not a rubric matter.

notes: The honest-absence semantics are already modelled in the schema (amountUndisclosed vs zero; isRolling; open_status) - this case ensures the reasoning layer preserves them through to prose. The data floor's hardest-won distinctions die here if the prompt is careless.
